title: The poster that spelled the shop wrong
scenario:
A bookshop called Quillon Books holds an author night. You make the poster with image models. Your teammate tried three tools and wrote down what happened.

Use the exhibit. The shop, the prompts and the notes are made up for this case. The field names are from the vendors' docs in October 2026.
exhibit:
BRIEF (made up)
  Headline:  QUILLON NIGHTS
  Line 2:    Author night, Friday 8pm
  Font:      the shop uses Garamond Premier on its sign

TRY 1, OpenAI GPT Image 2.5
  Prompt: "Poster for a bookshop author night with the headline Quillon Nights and the date"
  Note:   headline came out as "QUILON NIGHTS"; a second, made-up slogan appeared at the bottom.

TRY 2, Ideogram 4.5, JSON element (part)
  { "type": "text", "bbox": [40, 80, 180, 920], "text": "QUILLON NIGHTS", "desc": "Garamond Premier, cream" }
  Note:   placement good; the letters look like a generic serif, not the sign.

TRY 3, Recraft V3, text_layout (part)
  [ { "text": "Author night", "bbox": [40, 80, 180, 920] } ]

questions.prompt: Try 1 misspelled the shop and added a slogan. Which rewrite follows OpenAI's guide best?

options.text: Headline "QUILLON NIGHTS" (Q-U-I-L-L-O-N), no text besides it and the date line
options.explanation: Right. The OpenAI docs say to quote the wording, spell brand names letter by letter, and ask for no extra text.

options.text: The headline Quillon Nights in big letters, and make it really, really clear
options.explanation: The words are not in quotes and not spelled out, and nothing stops the extra slogan.

options.text: Any headline about books and nights that fits the poster, in a nice serif
options.explanation: This gives up the exact wording. The brief needs the shop's name spelled right.

options.text: The headline QUILLON NIGHTS, then a list of slogans the model may add too
options.explanation: This invites more text. The OpenAI docs say to ask for no extra text and then check the output.

questions.prompt: Try 2: the client wants the exact Garamond Premier look from the sign. What is the best plan?

options.text: Keep the font name in desc, since Ideogram loads the named font file
options.explanation: The Ideogram docs say the model doesn't load real fonts and you can't pick a font by name.

options.text: Describe the letters in desc, and set the exact font in a design tool
options.explanation: Right. The Ideogram docs say to describe weight, shape and mood instead of a font name. An exact brand font is a design-tool job.

options.text: Move the font name to the start of the prompt, so it carries more weight
options.explanation: Text early helps the words to render, but Ideogram still cannot load a named font.

options.text: Add the font name to the palette list, next to the hex colours in JSON
options.explanation: color_palette holds hex colours only. It cannot carry a font.

questions.prompt: Try 3 copied the Ideogram box into Recraft. Why will that box not work there as it is?

options.text: Recraft boxes use pixels, so the numbers must be the image's real size
options.explanation: Recraft's coordinates are relative, with (0, 0) top-left and (1, 1) bottom-right, not pixels.

options.text: Recraft boxes use the same order but need a scale from 0 to 100
options.explanation: Recraft does not use Ideogram's order or a 0–100 scale. It uses four [x, y] points from 0 to 1.

options.text: Recraft takes four [x, y] corner points from 0 to 1, not y-first edges
options.explanation: Right. The Ideogram docs use [y_min, x_min, y_max, x_max] from 0 to 1000. Recraft wants four points, x first, relative from 0 to 1.

options.text: Recraft boxes only work when the image is square, so set 1:1 first
options.explanation: Recraft's text layout page does not limit boxes to square images.

questions.prompt: Try 3 also puts "Author night" in one text_layout entry. What does Recraft's reference say about that?

options.text: It is fine: each entry can hold a full line of text with spaces
options.explanation: The Recraft docs say the text field must be a single word.

options.text: Each entry is one word, so "Author" and "night" need their own box
options.explanation: Right. Recraft's text layout says each element is an individual word with its own bounding box.

options.text: It works, but only if the line is placed in the middle of the image
options.explanation: Position is not the problem. The text field must hold a single word.

options.text: Text layout is for Recraft V4 only, so the model must change first
options.explanation: It is the other way round: the Recraft docs say text layout works on V3 and V3 Vector only.
